title: Why It Still Matters: the Civil War's legacy

segments.text: The Civil War ended slavery and remade America.
The Fourteenth promised equal protection under the law.
The Fifteenth protected the right to vote.
During Reconstruction, Black Americans voted in huge numbers,
and were elected to Congress and state governments.
The federal government became stronger, and the Union permanent.
It was also the first industrial war,
A preview of what the world would see in nineteen fourteen.
But Reconstruction ended in eighteen seventy-seven,
and the struggle for equality went on for another century.
The unfinished work of the Civil War shaped the civil rights movement.
